lede:divided-kingdom@a6fa0e.note: The split, Samaria, Jerusalem, the prophets and Assyria's removal of Israel are stated. 'North' and 'south' are geographic glosses these verses do not state.

lede:early-church@1fe961.note: Pentecost, the witness from Jerusalem through Judaea and Samaria, and arrival in Rome are stated. 'Roman world' is a gloss; Acts 1:8 says 'the uttermost part of the earth'.

lede:exiles@19605c.note: The burning of the house, Judah's exile and Daniel's faithfulness and looking for return are stated. Ezekiel's obedience is shown (ezek.2.7), but not that he looked for return; only God's promise to him is stated (ezek.37.12).

lede:exodus@f78663.note: The sea crossing, the arrival at Sinai, the law, the forty years and the view of the land are all stated.

lede:israel-in-egypt@f95517.note: Joseph's rule, the settlement in Goshen, the growth of the family, the new Pharaoh and the bondage are all stated.

lede:judges@b003a8.note: The Jordan crossing, the drift after Joshua, and the judges Deborah, Gideon and Samson are all stated.

lede:life-of-christ@ef552d.note: Birth in Bethlehem, growing up in Nazareth, teaching and healing in Galilee, the journey to Jerusalem, death and rising are all stated.

lede:patriarchs@a762fc.note: Ur, the call with land, nation and blessing, and the wandering in Canaan are stated. Genesis places the call after the family reaches Haran (gen.11.31-12.1); Acts 7:2-4 places it in Mesopotamia.

lede:return@29268d.note: Cyrus's release, the finished temple, Ezra's teaching of the law (ezra.7.10) and the walls under Nehemiah are stated. 'Again' is a gloss: the text does not say the law had been lost.

lede:united-kingdom-era@e8c0fb.note: Saul is king over Israel (1sam.13.1), but the text does not say he ruled all twelve tribes. 'Capital' is a gloss for David dwelling in Zion (2sam.5.9). The rest is stated.
